classes.objetivo: Reconocer en el habla de un entrenador si una frase es instrucción, ánimo o retroalimentación, y distinguir cuándo dirige y cuándo apoya.

ensenanza.en: A good coach will give instructions in short, clear sentences: pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
ensenanza.es: Un buen entrenador da instrucciones en frases cortas y claras: pasa el balón antes y mantén tu posición.
ensenanza.nota: Instrucción: imperativo directo que dice qué hacer ahora.

ensenanza.en: I love your effort today; you never gave up, and that is what will encourage the younger players most.
ensenanza.es: Me encanta tu esfuerzo de hoy; nunca te rendiste, y eso es lo que más animará a los jugadores más jóvenes.
ensenanza.nota: Ánimo: reconoce el esfuerzo y motiva, sin dar órdenes.

ensenanza.en: Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half, so that is what we should improve.
ensenanza.es: Tu punto fuerte es la velocidad, pero tus pases llegaron tarde en la segunda parte, así que eso es lo que debemos mejorar.
ensenanza.nota: Retroalimentación: un punto fuerte + un dato concreto + algo que mejorar.

ensenanza.en: Keep going, you are doing great under pressure, and I want you to shoot as soon as you see the space.
ensenanza.es: Sigue así, lo estás haciendo genial bajo presión, y quiero que dispares en cuanto veas el espacio.
ensenanza.nota: Ánimo e instrucción pueden ir juntos: Keep going motiva y shoot dice qué hacer.

ensenanza.en: The coach gave us some feedback after the match: constructive criticism names one concrete thing and ends with a next step.
ensenanza.es: El entrenador nos dio algunos comentarios tras el partido: la crítica constructiva nombra una cosa concreta y termina con un siguiente paso.
ensenanza.nota: Feedback no tiene plural: some feedback, a lot of feedback.

ensenanza.en: Before the final, the coach gave a short pep talk that made everybody feel calmer and more confident.
ensenanza.es: Antes de la final, el entrenador dio una breve charla de ánimo que hizo que todos se sintieran más tranquilos y seguros.
ensenanza.nota: Una pep talk es una charla corta para motivar al equipo justo antes de competir.

explicacion.texto: Un buen líder combina tres tipos de lenguaje. La instrucción usa el imperativo y dice qué hacer ahora: Pass the ball sooner. El ánimo reconoce el esfuerzo y motiva: I love your effort, Keep going. La retroalimentación mira hacia atrás y hacia adelante: nombra un punto fuerte, un dato concreto y algo que mejorar. Para clasificar una frase, fíjate en el verbo (¿orden, elogio o descripción de lo que pasó?) y en el tono. Cuando nadie da un dato, el comentario suele ser solo ánimo.

formula.nota: punto fuerte: reconoce lo que funciona

formula.texto: but your passes were late in the second half,
so try looking up before you pass.

erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Early es corto: su comparativo es earlier, no more early; y para dar la orden basta el verbo pass.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I want to give you a feedback.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I want to give you some feedback.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Feedback es incontable: no lleva a ni plural; se dice some feedback o a piece of feedback.

situacion.contexto: Mia habla con el entrenador Carlos después del partido.

dialogo.texto: Coach, what did you think of my game?
dialogo.traduccion: Entrenador, ¿qué le pareció mi partido?

dialogo.texto: I love your effort today. Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late.
dialogo.traduccion: Me encantó tu esfuerzo de hoy. Tu punto fuerte es la velocidad, pero tus pases llegaron tarde.

dialogo.texto: So I should improve my passing?
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces, ¿debo mejorar mis pases?

dialogo.texto: Yes. Look up before you pass. You are doing great!
dialogo.traduccion: Sí. Levanta la vista antes de pasar. ¡Lo estás haciendo genial!

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué frase de Carlos es retroalimentación y no solo ánimo ni instrucción?

opciones.es: «Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late.»

item.feedback: Esa frase nombra un punto fuerte y un dato concreto sobre lo que salió mal: es retroalimentación.

filas.texto: Your strength is your speed, but you can improve your passing.

guiada.consigna: ¿Cuál de estas frases es una instrucción directa del entrenador?
guiada.feedback: La instrucción usa el imperativo (pass, stay) y dice qué hacer ahora; las otras animan o valoran.
opciones: Pass the ball sooner and stay in your position.
I love your effort; you never gave up today.
Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late.
guiada.pista: Busca la frase que empieza con un verbo en imperativo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Tu punto fuerte es tu velocidad, pero tus pases llegaron tarde.»
guiada.feedback: Strength es el punto fuerte: la retroalimentación útil empieza reconociendo lo que funciona.
guiada.texto: The coach did not shout at the team. She simply told Mia: Your ___ is your speed, but your passes were late in the second half.
guiada.pista: Es el sustantivo de «punto fuerte»; empieza por str-.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Sigue así, lo estás haciendo genial bajo presión.»
guiada.feedback: Keep going y You are doing great motivan; under pressure cierra la frase.
guiada.respuesta: Keep going you are doing great under pressure
guiada.pista: Empieza con Keep going y termina con under pressure.

practica.consigna: Escucha la charla del descanso y elige qué función tiene «I love your effort today».
practica.feedback: «I love your effort» reconoce el esfuerzo de Mia sin dar órdenes ni datos: es ánimo.
practica.audio: At half-time, the coach spoke to the players. Pass the ball sooner, she told Leo, and stay in your position. Then she turned to Mia. I love your effort today, she said, you never gave up. Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the first half, so try looking up before you pass. The team was losing two to nothing, but nobody looked worried. Keep going, the coach added: you are doing great under pressure.
opciones: It recognises her effort without giving her an order.
It tells her exactly what to change in the second half.
It gives her a fact about how the game is going.

practica.consigna: Con la misma charla, elige qué se le pide a Mia que haga distinto.
practica.feedback: La mejora para Mia es mirar antes de pasar; pasar antes y mantener la posición era la instrucción para Leo.
practica.audio: At half-time, the coach spoke to the players. Pass the ball sooner, she told Leo, and stay in your position. Then she turned to Mia. I love your effort today, she said, you never gave up. Your strength is your speed, but your passes were late in the first half, so try looking up before you pass. The team was losing two to nothing, but nobody looked worried. Keep going, the coach added: you are doing great under pressure.
opciones: To look up before she passes the ball.
To pass the ball sooner and stay in her position.
To shoot as soon as she sees the space.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase del entrenador con su función.
practica.feedback: La instrucción dice qué hacer, el ánimo reconoce el esfuerzo y la retroalimentación describe un hecho concreto.
pares: Shoot as soon as you see the space.
You never gave up today, well done!
Your passes were late in the second half.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué actitud adopta la entrenadora con el jugador.
evaluacion.feedback: Elogia su valentía y su esfuerzo y señala un único punto concreto: apoyo con una mejora clara.
evaluacion.audio: After the match, the coach sat next to a player who had missed an easy chance. She did not raise her voice. You were brave to try to score, she said, and your effort was the best in the team. The decision was late, though, so next time try looking at the goal before you shoot. Then she smiled. I want you to shoot again on Saturday.
opciones: She supports him while giving one clear point to improve.
She insists that the miss was bad luck and that nothing needs to change.
She praises his courage but avoids saying anything specific about the mistake.

evaluacion.consigna: Con el mismo relato, elige por qué dice «I want you to shoot again on Saturday».
evaluacion.feedback: Pedirle que vuelva a disparar demuestra confianza: el fallo no cambia lo que espera de él.
evaluacion.audio: After the match, the coach sat next to a player who had missed an easy chance. She did not raise her voice. You were brave to try to score, she said, and your effort was the best in the team. The decision was late, though, so next time try looking at the goal before you shoot. Then she smiled. I want you to shoot again on Saturday.
opciones: To show that she still trusts him after the mistake.
To give him an order about his new position.
To warn him that he will be tested on Saturday.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Prefieren la crítica constructiva: una cosa concreta y un siguiente paso.»
evaluacion.feedback: Constructive criticism es la crítica que señala un punto concreto y propone un siguiente paso.
evaluacion.texto: Good coaches avoid vague comments like That was bad. They prefer ___ criticism: one concrete thing and a next step.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Levanta la vista antes de pasar el balón.»
evaluacion.feedback: La instrucción va en imperativo y sitúa la condición con before.
evaluacion.respuesta: Look up before you pass the ball

repaso.consigna: Lee el mensaje del entrenador y elige con qué propósito lo escribe.
repaso.feedback: El mensaje nombra un punto fuerte (correr), un dato concreto (pérdidas en el medio) y un paso siguiente: retroalimentación.
opciones: To give feedback that recognises a strength and proposes a next step.
To encourage the team and avoid talking about any mistakes.
To complain that the players do not run enough and to ask for extra running.
repaso.texto: Coach's message to the team: Good work tonight. I know you are tired. Your strength this season is how hard you run, but we lose the ball too often in the middle of the pitch. On Thursday, let's practise short passes. See you at six.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué quiere enseñar el entrenador con sus palabras.
repaso.feedback: El entrenador sustituye el grito por frases claras y tranquilas: «Pass to me» en lugar de culpar.
repaso.audio: During a training session, a young player kept shouting at his teammates. The coach stopped the practice and said quietly: Encourage, don't blame. When you shout, people get tense and pass the ball too fast. Next time, say what you need: I'm open, or Pass to me. Try it now.
opciones: That clear, calm instructions help more than shouting does.
That players should never talk during training.
That only the coach is allowed to give instructions.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Sus comentarios nos mostraron cómo mejorar nuestros pases.»
repaso.feedback: Improve significa mejorar; la retroalimentación útil enseña en qué y cómo hacerlo.
repaso.texto: We were losing every game until the coach's comments showed us exactly how we could ___ our passing.

classes.objetivo: Formular preguntas de coaching abiertas e hipotéticas (What would it take to...?, What's stopping you from...?) en lugar de dar consejos directos.

ensenanza.en: A coach rarely gives advice; instead she asks, What would it take to reach a goal that you set for this month?
ensenanza.es: Un coach rara vez da consejos; en cambio pregunta: ¿qué haría falta para alcanzar una meta que te fijaste para este mes?
ensenanza.nota: What would it take to + verbo: pregunta abierta sobre lo necesario.

ensenanza.en: What is the biggest obstacle for you right now, and which option feels more realistic given your week?
ensenanza.es: ¿Cuál es el mayor obstáculo para ti ahora mismo, y qué opción te parece más realista dada tu semana?
ensenanza.nota: Pregunta abierta con What y Which: no se contesta con sí o no.

ensenanza.en: How would you feel if you could make progress this week, and what would make you more confident?
ensenanza.es: ¿Cómo te sentirías si pudieras avanzar esta semana, y qué te haría sentirte más seguro?
ensenanza.nota: Pregunta hipotética: would + if + pasado simple (could).

ensenanza.en: What would you do if you were more confident, and what small first step could you take tomorrow morning?
ensenanza.es: ¿Qué harías si fueras más seguro de ti mismo, y qué pequeño primer paso podrías dar mañana por la mañana?
ensenanza.nota: If + pasado simple (were) imagina un escenario; take a step = dar un paso.

ensenanza.en: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group, and what might hold back your best ideas?
ensenanza.es: ¿Qué te impide hablar delante del grupo, y qué podría frenar tus mejores ideas?
ensenanza.nota: What's stopping you from + -ing: busca el obstáculo real.

ensenanza.en: A good question can reveal a blind spot or push you out of your comfort zone, so ask it as a real option, not a hidden order.
ensenanza.es: Una buena pregunta puede revelar un punto ciego o sacarte de tu zona de confort, así que formúlala como una opción real, no como una orden encubierta.
ensenanza.nota: Evita Why don't you...?: suena a pregunta, pero es un consejo disfrazado.

explicacion.texto: Un coach no da la solución: hace preguntas para que la otra persona la encuentre. Son abiertas (empiezan por What o How y no se responden con sí o no) y a menudo hipotéticas: What would it take to...? What would you do if...? What's stopping you from...? Evita Why don't you...?, que es un consejo disfrazado. Para convertir un consejo en pregunta, cambia You should practise daily por What would help you practise daily?

formula.nota: What would it take: «¿qué haría falta?»
la meta de la otra persona

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: What would it take for reach your goal?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: What would it take to reach your goal?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de take va to + verbo base; for + infinitivo es un calco de «para».

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: What is stopping you to speak?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: What is stopping you from speaking?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Stop you from va seguido de -ing: from speaking.

situacion.contexto: La entrenadora Sara habla con Tom, que quiere hablar delante del grupo pero nunca lo hace.

dialogo.texto: I want to speak in front of the group, but I never do.
dialogo.traduccion: Quiero hablar delante del grupo, pero nunca lo hago.

dialogo.texto: What's stopping you from speaking?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Qué te impide hablar?

dialogo.texto: I am not confident. I worry about mistakes.
dialogo.traduccion: No me siento seguro. Me preocupan los errores.

dialogo.texto: What would it take to feel more confident?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Qué haría falta para sentirte más seguro?

dialogo.texto: Maybe a small first step, like speaking for one minute.
dialogo.traduccion: Quizá un pequeño primer paso, como hablar un minuto.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué hace Sara en lugar de dar un consejo?

opciones.es: Hace preguntas abiertas para que Tom nombre su obstáculo y su primer paso.
Le dice exactamente qué debe decir ante el grupo.
Le recomienda que deje de hablar en público.

item.feedback: Sara pregunta «What's stopping you...?» y «What would it take...?»: Tom encuentra solo su obstáculo y su primer paso.

filas.texto: What would it take to talk to her?
What's stopping you from feeling calm?
What could you try to practise more?

guiada.consigna: ¿Cuál de estas es una pregunta de coaching abierta, no un consejo ni un sí o no?
guiada.feedback: Solo «What would it take…?» es abierta: no se responde con sí o no ni esconde un consejo.
opciones: What would it take to reach a goal this month?
Do you think you can reach your goal this month?
Why don't you just set a smaller goal this month?
guiada.pista: Descarta la que se responde con sí o no y la que suena a consejo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «¿Qué te impide hablar delante del grupo?»
guiada.feedback: What's stopping you from + -ing busca el obstáculo real que frena a la persona.
guiada.texto: The player says that she wants to be more confident. Her coach answers with a question instead of advice: What's ___ you from speaking in front of the group?
guiada.pista: Es el verbo en -ing que va antes de you from.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «¿Qué harías si fueras más seguro de ti mismo?»
guiada.feedback: La pregunta hipotética une would en la principal con el pasado simple (were) tras if.
guiada.respuesta: What would you do if you were more confident
guiada.pista: Empieza con What would you do y usa were tras if.

practica.consigna: Escucha la sesión y elige qué hace la entrenadora en lugar de dar un consejo.
practica.feedback: La entrenadora pregunta en vez de aconsejar, y así él mismo nombra su problema (el miedo a equivocarse).
practica.audio: A volunteer coach was talking to a boy who wanted to join the school team but kept finding excuses. She did not tell him to try harder. Instead, she asked: What's stopping you from going to the first training? He said he was afraid of making mistakes in front of the others. So she asked another question: What would it take for you to feel more confident? After a pause he answered that he could ask a friend to come with him. The coach simply smiled.
opciones: She asks questions that help him name his own problem.
She explains why mistakes are part of the game.
She warns him that the school team will not wait.

practica.consigna: Con la misma sesión, elige qué sugiere la sonrisa final de la entrenadora.
practica.feedback: Sonríe porque la solución (llevar a un amigo) la encontró él: es lo que busca una pregunta de coaching.
practica.audio: A volunteer coach was talking to a boy who wanted to join the school team but kept finding excuses. She did not tell him to try harder. Instead, she asked: What's stopping you from going to the first training? He said he was afraid of making mistakes in front of the others. So she asked another question: What would it take for you to feel more confident? After a pause he answered that he could ask a friend to come with him. The coach simply smiled.
opciones: That the idea came from him, which is exactly what she hoped for.
That she thinks his plan is too simple for him.
That she had already decided to invite his friend.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Es más fácil hallar una solución cuando puedes nombrar el mayor obstáculo.»
practica.feedback: Obstacle es lo que se interpone en el camino; nombrarlo es el primer paso de una buena pregunta de coaching.
practica.texto: Most people already know part of the answer. It is easier to find a solution once you can name the biggest ___ in your way.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe dos preguntas de coaching para que el jugador supere su miedo.
evaluacion.feedback: Dos preguntas abiertas, una sobre el obstáculo (What's stopping you from...?) y otra hipotética (What would it take...?), sin dar consejos.
evaluacion.texto: Un jugador te dice: «Quiero hablar delante del grupo, pero me paralizo.» No le des consejos. Escribe dos preguntas abiertas: una con What's stopping you from... y otra con What would it take...
evaluacion.respuesta: What's stopping you from speaking in front of the group? What would it take for you to feel more confident?
aceptadas: What is stopping you from speaking in front of the group? What would it take to be more confident?
What's stopping you from speaking in front of the others? What would it take for you to be more confident?

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué funcionó mejor el segundo entrenador.
evaluacion.feedback: La jugadora encuentra su propia solución (usar el descanso); al primero solo le dieron órdenes y no hizo nada.
evaluacion.audio: Two coaches talked to the same player. The first said: You should practise every day, and you should stop worrying. The player nodded but did nothing. The second asked: What would help you to practise three times this week? The player thought for a moment, then said she could use her lunch break. She wrote it down and looked surprised at how simple it was.
opciones: The player found her own solution instead of receiving orders.
The second coach set a more ambitious target than the first coach.
The player trusted the second coach more because that coach was more experienced.

evaluacion.consigna: Con la misma escena, elige qué sugiere que la jugadora «looked surprised».
evaluacion.feedback: La sorpresa se refiere a lo simple que era la solución, no al desacuerdo ni al esfuerzo requerido.
evaluacion.audio: Two coaches talked to the same player. The first said: You should practise every day, and you should stop worrying. The player nodded but did nothing. The second asked: What would help you to practise three times this week? The player thought for a moment, then said she could use her lunch break. She wrote it down and looked surprised at how simple it was.
opciones: That she had not expected to find an answer so easily.
That she disagreed with the question that the coach had asked.
That she was shocked by how much practice was needed.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «¿Qué haría falta para hablar con ella?»
evaluacion.feedback: What would it take to + verbo es la pregunta abierta que sustituye al consejo disfrazado.
evaluacion.texto: Why don't you talk to her? sounds like a question, but it is really advice in disguise. A better version is: What would it ___ to talk to her?

repaso.consigna: Lee lo que dice el adolescente y elige la respuesta que es una pregunta de coaching.
repaso.feedback: Solo «What's stopping you…?» es una pregunta abierta; las otras son consejos, aunque una suene a pregunta.
opciones: What's stopping you from finishing one small thing this week?
You should finish one small thing every week, starting today.
Why don't you ask a friend to check your work every day?
repaso.texto: A boy tells his coach: I never finish anything, and I do not know why.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige con qué fin hace la entrenadora la segunda pregunta.
repaso.feedback: La segunda pregunta parte de la emoción de la jugadora y busca convertirla en algo útil, sin juzgarla.
repaso.audio: At the end of the session, the coach asked the team: How would you feel if we won the next match? Nobody answered at first. Then the youngest player said that she would feel proud, but also nervous. The coach wrote both words on the board and asked: What would help us turn the nervous feeling into energy?
opciones: To help the players turn their worry into something useful.
To reassure the youngest player that there is nothing to be nervous about.
To move the conversation away from winning the match.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «¿Qué opción es más realista esta semana: una sesión larga o tres cortas?»
repaso.feedback: Realistic describe lo que se puede cumplir en la práctica; una buena pregunta ayuda a elegir una opción realista.
repaso.texto: You cannot do everything at once. Which option feels more ___ for you this week: one long session or three short ones?

classes.objetivo: Valorar si una retroalimentación es específica, respetuosa y accionable, y decidir qué habría que mejorar en las que no lo son.

vocabulario.es: accionable; que se puede poner en práctica

ensenanza.en: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, which is a specific observation that anyone on the pitch could confirm.
ensenanza.es: Me fijé en que hiciste con prisa tus dos últimos pases, y esa es una observación concreta que cualquiera en el campo podría confirmar.
ensenanza.nota: Específica: describe un hecho que se vio, no una opinión.

ensenanza.en: That was terrible, and you never listen to anybody: that kind of comment is disrespectful, and it does not tell you what to do next.
ensenanza.es: Eso fue terrible y nunca escuchas a nadie: ese tipo de comentario es irrespetuoso y no te dice qué hacer después.
ensenanza.nota: Irrespetuosa: ataca a la persona con terrible y never, y no dice qué hacer.

ensenanza.en: Next time, breathe before you shoot and stay calm, because a steady start gives you more time to choose your shot.
ensenanza.es: La próxima vez, respira antes de disparar y mantén la calma, porque un comienzo sereno te da más tiempo para elegir tu tiro.
ensenanza.nota: Accionable: Next time + imperativo = un paso que se puede dar.

ensenanza.en: I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week; that is an actionable step, because you can start it tomorrow.
ensenanza.es: Te sugiero que practiques tu pie izquierdo dos veces por semana; es un paso accionable, porque puedes empezarlo mañana.
ensenanza.nota: I suggest you + verbo base: sugerencia concreta, sin to.

ensenanza.en: Your talk was helpful because you gave clear examples, and your respectful tone made it easy for the group to listen.
ensenanza.es: Tu charla fue útil porque diste ejemplos claros, y tu tono respetuoso hizo que al grupo le resultara fácil escuchar.
ensenanza.nota: Valorar con un motivo: because + dato concreto.

ensenanza.en: "That was good, I guess" is only a vague comment, so ask politely: could you be more specific about what worked?
ensenanza.es: «Estuvo bien, supongo» es solo un comentario vago, así que pregunta con educación: ¿podrías ser más concreto sobre qué funcionó?
ensenanza.nota: Ante un comentario vago, pide concreción con Could you be more specific?

explicacion.texto: Para valorar un comentario, aplica tres criterios. ¿Es específico? Cita un hecho (I noticed that you rushed...) en lugar de una impresión (You did fine). ¿Es respetuoso? Habla de lo que se hizo, no de cómo es la persona (nada de You never listen). ¿Es accionable? Propone algo que se pueda hacer (Next time, breathe before you shoot). Un comentario vago o irrespetuoso puede sonar sincero, pero no ayuda a mejorar. Al escuchar, pregúntate qué criterio falta.

formula.texto: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes,

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I suggest you to practise more.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de suggest you va el verbo base sin to; también se puede decir suggest that you practise.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I noticed you rush your passes yesterday.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I noticed you rushed your passes yesterday.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Para hablar de algo que ya pasó, noticed va con un verbo en pasado: rushed.

situacion.contexto: Mia quiere saber qué le pareció su charla al entrenador Carlos.

dialogo.texto: Coach said that my talk was good, I guess.
dialogo.traduccion: El entrenador dijo que mi charla estuvo bien, supongo.

dialogo.texto: That is a vague comment. Can you ask him to be more specific?
dialogo.traduccion: Ese es un comentario vago. ¿Puedes pedirle que sea más concreto?

dialogo.texto: Coach, what exactly was helpful?
dialogo.traduccion: Entrenador, ¿qué fue exactamente lo útil?

dialogo.texto: I noticed that you gave clear examples. Next time, breathe before you start.
dialogo.traduccion: Me fijé en que diste ejemplos claros. La próxima vez, respira antes de empezar.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué hace Mia para conseguir una retroalimentación útil?

opciones.es: Pide concreción: pregunta qué fue exactamente lo útil de su charla.
Acepta el comentario vago sin preguntar nada más.
Le dice al entrenador que su comentario fue irrespetuoso.

item.feedback: Mia pregunta «what exactly was helpful?» y así consigue un dato concreto y un siguiente paso.

filas.texto: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes.
Your passes were rushed, but I know you can improve them.
I suggest you practise your left foot twice a week.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué comentario es específico y respetuoso a la vez?
guiada.feedback: Solo el comentario sobre los dos últimos pases cita un hecho concreto sin juzgar a la persona.
opciones: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes.
You always rush everything you do on the pitch.
That was not very good, but I am sure you will improve.
guiada.pista: Busca el que cita un hecho que se vio, sin always ni never.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «“Estuvo bien, supongo” es un comentario vago: no dice qué repetir.»
guiada.feedback: Un comentario vago suena amable, pero no cita ningún hecho ni dice qué hacer.
guiada.texto: That was good, I guess is a ___ comment: it does not tell you what to repeat or what to change.
guiada.pista: Es el adjetivo contrario a specific.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «La próxima vez, respira antes de disparar y mantén la calma.»
guiada.feedback: Next time + imperativo es la estructura de un paso accionable.
guiada.respuesta: Next time breathe before you shoot and stay calm
guiada.pista: Empieza por Next time y acaba con stay calm.

practica.consigna: Escucha los comentarios del entrenador y elige cuál es específico y accionable.
practica.feedback: Solo el segundo comentario cita un hecho (pases apresurados) y un paso que se puede dar (respirar antes de pasar).
practica.audio: After the tournament, three players received comments from their coach. To the first he said: That was terrible, you never listen. To the second he said: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, so next time, breathe before you pass and stay calm. To the third he said: That was good, I guess. The third player looked confused and asked: Could you be more specific? The coach thought for a moment and answered: Your talk to the group was helpful because you gave clear examples.
opciones: The one about the rushed passes and breathing before the next pass.
The one that says the talk was good, I guess.
The one that says that the player never listens to anybody at all.

practica.consigna: Con los mismos comentarios, elige qué hace el tercer jugador para mejorar lo que recibe.
practica.feedback: El tercer jugador pide concreción con «Could you be more specific?» y consigue un motivo claro.
practica.audio: After the tournament, three players received comments from their coach. To the first he said: That was terrible, you never listen. To the second he said: I noticed that you rushed your last two passes, so next time, breathe before you pass and stay calm. To the third he said: That was good, I guess. The third player looked confused and asked: Could you be more specific? The coach thought for a moment and answered: Your talk to the group was helpful because you gave clear examples.
opciones: He asks the coach to be more specific.
He tells the coach that the comment was disrespectful.
He accepts the comment and thanks the coach.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada comentario con el criterio que incumple o cumple.
practica.feedback: El primero ataca a la persona, el segundo no cita ningún hecho y el tercero describe algo comprobable.
pares: I noticed that you lost the ball three times.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué fue útil el comentario de Leo.
evaluacion.feedback: Leo cita un hecho (habló rápido en el medio) y propone pasos (respirar, añadir un ejemplo): específico y accionable.
evaluacion.audio: At the volunteer meeting, Sara gave a short presentation. Afterwards, her manager said: That was confusing. Leo, who was sitting next to her, tried again: I noticed that you spoke quickly in the middle, so next time, take a breath before each new idea, and I suggest you add one example. Sara nodded.
opciones: It described what he noticed and gave her a step to take.
It compared her presentation with the ones given by other volunteers.
It praised her for speaking quickly and clearly.

evaluacion.consigna: Con la misma escena, elige qué se deduce del comentario del jefe «That was confusing».
evaluacion.feedback: «Confusing» expresa una impresión sin decir qué cambiar; no ataca a Sara ni propone un paso concreto.
evaluacion.audio: At the volunteer meeting, Sara gave a short presentation. Afterwards, her manager said: That was confusing. Leo, who was sitting next to her, tried again: I noticed that you spoke quickly in the middle, so next time, take a breath before each new idea, and I suggest you add one example. Sara nodded.
opciones: It is vague: it gives an impression but not what to change.
It is disrespectful because it judges Sara as a person, not her presentation.
It is useful because it tells her to explain more.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Un comentario es accionable cuando propone un paso que puedes dar mañana.»
evaluacion.feedback: Actionable describe lo que se puede poner en práctica de inmediato: un paso concreto, no un deseo general.
evaluacion.texto: Telling someone You need to improve does not help much. A comment is ___ only when it names a step that you can take tomorrow.

evaluacion.consigna: Lee el correo y elige qué criterio incumple principalmente.
evaluacion.feedback: El correo sí dice cuánto llegó tarde (veinte minutos); lo que falla es que juzga la actitud de Tom.
opciones: It is disrespectful: it judges Tom's attitude instead of describing facts.
It is vague: it never says how late Tom was.
It is too long and gives Tom several tasks at once.
evaluacion.texto: Email to a volunteer: Hi Tom, you were twenty minutes late, again. You clearly do not care about this project. Please fix this.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la niña sobre el comentario «Try harder».
repaso.feedback: «Try harder» no dice qué cambiar; el nuevo comentario sí (frenar al final), y por eso le motiva.
repaso.audio: A coach told a girl: Your start was fast, but you rushed the final part. Tomorrow, let's practise slowing down together. The girl smiled. At her old club, the coach only said: Try harder. She told her mother that this new feedback was the first that made her want to train.
opciones: That it was vague and did not tell her how to improve.
That it was disrespectful and made her leave the old club at once.
That it was too specific for a player of her age.

repaso.consigna: Lee la situación y elige la versión mejorada del comentario «Good job».
repaso.feedback: La versión mejorada cita un hecho y propone un paso; las otras son elogio vago o ataque.
opciones: Good job: I noticed that you answered every question calmly; next time, add an example.
Good job, you are clearly the best speaker in the whole group, and everyone knows it.
Good job, but your answers were terrible in the middle.
repaso.texto: A manager wants to improve the comment Good job, which she wrote after a colleague's interview. She wants it to be specific and actionable, but still respectful.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Te sugiero que practiques tu pie izquierdo dos veces por semana.»
repaso.feedback: I suggest you + verbo base formula una recomendación concreta sin ser una orden.
repaso.texto: The coach does not give an order. She says, in a calm and respectful voice: I ___ you practise your left foot twice a week.

classes.objetivo: Ofrecer retroalimentación tras una derrota: reconocer un esfuerzo concreto, señalar una crítica específica y cerrar con el siguiente paso como pregunta de coaching.

ensenanza.en: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed, because we all wanted this final so much.
ensenanza.es: Sé que la derrota duele y que tienen todo el derecho a sentirse decepcionados, porque todos queríamos tanto esta final.
ensenanza.nota: Empieza reconociendo la emoción: así te escuchan antes de oír la crítica.

ensenanza.en: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half, and I want us to learn from what worked.
ensenanza.es: A pesar de la derrota, estoy orgulloso de cómo defendieron en la segunda parte, y quiero que aprendamos de lo que funcionó.
ensenanza.nota: Despite + sustantivo (sin of); proud of + el esfuerzo concreto.

ensenanza.en: However, we lost the ball too often in the middle, and that is a fixable problem, not a disaster.
ensenanza.es: Sin embargo, perdimos el balón demasiadas veces en el medio, y ese es un problema que tiene arreglo, no un desastre.
ensenanza.nota: However + coma: una crítica concreta y limitada a una sola cosa.

ensenanza.en: After this setback, what will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday, and what could each of us try first?
ensenanza.es: Tras este contratiempo, ¿qué haría falta para recuperarnos el próximo sábado, y qué podría intentar primero cada uno?
ensenanza.nota: Pregunta de coaching que proyecta el siguiente paso.

ensenanza.en: This was a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort, because nobody on the pitch stopped running.
ensenanza.es: Fue un resultado duro, pero merecen reconocimiento por su esfuerzo, porque nadie en el campo dejó de correr.
ensenanza.nota: Deserve credit for: reconocer el esfuerzo aunque se pierda.

ensenanza.en: There is still room for improvement in how we defend corners, but the setback is temporary and the season is long.
ensenanza.es: Todavía hay margen de mejora en cómo defendemos los córners, pero el contratiempo es temporal y la temporada es larga.
ensenanza.nota: Setback: un problema temporal; ayuda a poner la derrota en perspectiva.

explicacion.titulo: Hablar al equipo tras una derrota
explicacion.texto: Tras perder, una charla de entrenador tiene tres partes. Primero reconoce la emoción y un esfuerzo concreto: I know the defeat hurts; I'm proud of how you defended. Después, una sola crítica específica con However: However, we lost the ball too often in the middle. Cierra con el siguiente paso en forma de pregunta de coaching: What will it take to bounce back next Saturday? No culpes a nadie ni digas que todo estuvo bien: combina reconocimiento, verdad y plan.

formula.texto: I'm proud of how you defended;
however, we lost the ball too often,
so what would help us keep it next week?

erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Proud va con of: proud of + sustantivo o -ing.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Despite of the defeat, I'm proud of you.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of you.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Despite no lleva of; se dice despite o in spite of.

situacion.contexto: Después de perder un partido, el entrenador Carlos habla con la capitana Mia.

dialogo.texto: I know the defeat hurts. I'm proud of how you defended, Mia.
dialogo.traduccion: Sé que la derrota duele. Estoy orgulloso de cómo defendiste, Mia.

dialogo.texto: Thanks, coach. But we lost the ball too often in the middle.
dialogo.traduccion: Gracias, entrenador. Pero perdimos el balón demasiadas veces en el medio.

dialogo.texto: True. However, that is fixable. What will it take to bounce back next Saturday?
dialogo.traduccion: Cierto. Sin embargo, eso tiene arreglo. ¿Qué haría falta para recuperarnos el próximo sábado?

dialogo.texto: We could practise short passes on Thursday.
dialogo.traduccion: Podríamos practicar pases cortos el jueves.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿cómo cierra Carlos su charla?

opciones.es: Con una pregunta de coaching sobre lo que hará falta para recuperarse el sábado.
Con una crítica dura a la defensa de todo el equipo.
Con la promesa de cambiar a todos los jugadores.

item.feedback: Carlos termina con «What will it take to bounce back...?»: una pregunta de coaching que proyecta el siguiente paso.

filas.texto: I'm proud of how you defended in the second half.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle.
What will it take to bounce back next Saturday?

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase reconoce la emoción del equipo antes de empezar a criticar?
guiada.feedback: Solo la frase sobre el dolor de la derrota reconoce la emoción sin negarla ni culpar.
opciones: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed.
We lost because you did not follow the plan that we agreed.
It was only a game, so nobody should feel disappointed about it today.
guiada.pista: Busca la que nombra lo que siente el equipo sin negarlo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Sin embargo, perdimos el balón demasiadas veces en el medio.»
guiada.feedback: However introduce la crítica concreta después del reconocimiento; va seguido de coma.
guiada.texto: The coach does not want to hide the truth, so she adds one limited criticism: ___, we lost the ball too often in the middle.
guiada.pista: Es el conector de contraste que empieza por H.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «A pesar de la derrota, estoy orgulloso de cómo defendieron.»
guiada.feedback: Despite va seguido de sustantivo (the defeat) y proud lleva of en su complemento.
guiada.respuesta: Despite the defeat I am proud of how you defended
guiada.pista: Empieza por Despite y termina con la acción que se reconoce.

practica.consigna: Escucha la charla y elige cómo abre la entrenadora su intervención.
practica.feedback: Empieza con la emoción («the defeat hurts»); la crítica llega después con However.
practica.audio: The final whistle went, and the players sat in silence. The coach sat in front of them. I know the defeat hurts, she said, and you have every right to feel disappointed. Then she looked at the captain. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. However, we lost the ball too often in the middle, and that is fixable. She paused. What will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday? Nobody answered, but a few players were already nodding.
opciones: By recognising how the players feel about the loss.
By pointing out the mistake that cost the match.
By praising the captain for the goals that she scored.

practica.consigna: Con la misma charla, elige qué sugiere que algunos jugadores asientan.
practica.feedback: Nadie responde, pero asentir indica que la pregunta les hace pensar en cómo recuperarse.
practica.audio: The final whistle went, and the players sat in silence. The coach sat in front of them. I know the defeat hurts, she said, and you have every right to feel disappointed. Then she looked at the captain. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. However, we lost the ball too often in the middle, and that is fixable. She paused. What will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday? Nobody answered, but a few players were already nodding.
opciones: They accept the challenge and start thinking about the next match.
They agree that the coach was unfair to the captain in the second half.
They believe that the defeat was nobody's fault.

practica.consigna: Escribe un reconocimiento concreto y una crítica con However.
practica.feedback: La frase combina un reconocimiento específico con una crítica concreta introducida por however.
practica.texto: Tu equipo perdió 3-2. Escribe una frase que reconozca un esfuerzo concreto (la velocidad en el ataque) y continúe con however y una crítica concreta (dejaron demasiado espacio atrás).
practica.respuesta: I am proud of how fast you attacked. However, we left too much space at the back.
aceptadas: I'm proud of your speed in attack; however, we left too much space behind us.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe la charla del entrenador tras la derrota.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena charla reconoce la emoción y dos esfuerzos concretos, hace una crítica específica con however y cierra con una pregunta de coaching.
evaluacion.texto: Tu equipo perdió 2–1 la final del barrio. Escribe la charla del entrenador (unas 200–250 palabras): reconoce la emoción y dos esfuerzos concretos (la defensa y el ánimo), señala una crítica concreta (por ejemplo, balones perdidos en el medio) y cierra con un plan formulado como pregunta de coaching.
evaluacion.respuesta:
Team, sit down for a moment. I know this defeat hurts, and it is fine to feel disappointed. I feel the same.
First, I want to say what I saw. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. Mia, your two tackles saved us three times, and Tom, you never stopped talking to the team. You deserve credit for that.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, and that gave them the chance to score. It is only one thing, and it is fixable. One match does not decide our season.
So let me ask you: what would it take for us to keep the ball longer next Saturday? What could we try in training on Thursday? I would like to hear two ideas from each of you.
Go home, rest, and come back ready to learn. I believe in this team.
aceptadas:
Everyone, come here. I know how painful this defeat is, and I understand you are disappointed. I am too.
I want to start with what worked. I'm proud of how you supported each other during the last twenty minutes. Leo, your effort in defence was excellent, and Sara, you encouraged everybody until the final whistle.
However, we waited too long before we shot, and they blocked our chances easily. That is one concrete thing to improve, and it is not a disaster.
Now, what would help us to use the whole field next week? What is stopping us from looking for the right side? What could we try first on Tuesday? Think about it tonight, and tell me tomorrow.
It was a tough day, but you deserve to be proud of your effort. We will bounce back, and I will be with you on Saturday.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el correo de la capitana y elige qué actitud muestra hacia la charla.
evaluacion.feedback: La capitana agradece la charla pero pide más detalle sobre los errores: le gusta y exige concreción.
evaluacion.audio: After the heavy defeat, the captain wrote an email to the coach. She said the talk had helped, but added that one sentence had stayed in her mind: It is only a setback. She explained that it had stopped her from blaming herself. In the same email she asked for more detail about the mistakes, because praise alone, she wrote, would not help the team improve.
opciones: She likes the talk but wants more concrete criticism too.
She values the talk, but she would prefer it to focus only on the positives.
She thinks the talk should have avoided any criticism.

evaluacion.consigna: Con el mismo correo, elige por qué menciona la frase «It is only a setback».
evaluacion.feedback: La frase la ayudó a dejar de culparse, pero ella sigue pidiendo detalles para mejorar: no olvidó la derrota.
evaluacion.audio: After the heavy defeat, the captain wrote an email to the coach. She said the talk had helped, but added that one sentence had stayed in her mind: It is only a setback. She explained that it had stopped her from blaming herself. In the same email she asked for more detail about the mistakes, because praise alone, she wrote, would not help the team improve.
opciones: Because it helped her stop blaming herself for the result.
Because it made her forget about the defeat entirely and stay calm.
Because it convinced her that nothing needed to change.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Una derrota es dura, pero los mejores equipos aprenden de ella.»
evaluacion.feedback: Learn from significa aprender de la experiencia; tras una derrota marca el paso de la queja al plan.
evaluacion.texto: Nobody enjoys losing a final. Even so, the best teams always ___ from a defeat, because it shows them exactly where to improve.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué contraste ilustra el relato entre las dos charlas.
repaso.feedback: La primera charla culpa y silencia; la segunda reconoce, critica un hecho y pregunta, y los jugadores hablan.
repaso.audio: After a two to one defeat, a coach said: That was a disaster, and you all know whose fault it was. The captain looked at the floor. A week later a different coach spoke to the same team after another loss: I'm proud of how you defended, however we lost the ball in the middle. What would help us keep it? The players talked about it all evening.
opciones: Blame closes the conversation, while specific recognition opens it.
Criticism should always be avoided after a defeat.
Replacing the coach improves the results of the team.

repaso.consigna: Lee la queja del jugador y elige la respuesta que reconoce, critica y propone un paso.
repaso.feedback: La respuesta combina reconocimiento (brave), una crítica concreta (ball away) y una pregunta de coaching.
opciones: You lost, but your second half was brave; however, we gave the ball away too often. What could we change?
You lost, so we have to work twice as hard from now on, and there will be no more excuses.
Nothing was good today, but the next match will surely be easier for all of us.
repaso.texto: After the match a player says to the coach: We lost, so nothing we did today was good, and I am tired of trying.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Tras este contratiempo, ¿qué haría falta para recuperarnos la próxima semana?»
repaso.feedback: Bounce back es recuperarse tras un contratiempo; la pregunta de coaching mira hacia adelante.
repaso.texto: Nobody is saying that the defeat does not matter. After this setback, what will it take for us to ___ back next week?

classes.objetivo: Guiar a un grupo de voluntarios por un cambio: explicar la razón, presentar el plan, ofrecer apoyo y responder a preocupaciones con preguntas de coaching.

vocabulario.es: a bordo; de acuerdo con el plan

ensenanza.en: I want to announce a change in our Saturday schedule, and I would like to explain why before I share the details.
ensenanza.es: Quiero anunciar un cambio en nuestro horario de los sábados, y me gustaría explicar por qué antes de dar los detalles.
ensenanza.nota: Anunciar: el inicio claro de un mensaje de cambio.

ensenanza.en: The reason is simple: more families are coming to the garden, and we need more time to welcome them properly.
ensenanza.es: El motivo es sencillo: vienen más familias al huerto y necesitamos más tiempo para recibirlas bien.
ensenanza.nota: The reason is...: explica el porqué antes de dar el plan.

ensenanza.en: Here is the plan: one morning shift and one afternoon shift, starting next month, and a review after four weeks to get everyone on board.
ensenanza.es: Este es el plan: un turno de mañana y uno de tarde, a partir del mes próximo, y una revisión a las cuatro semanas para que todos se sumen.
ensenanza.nota: Here is the plan: presenta los pasos concretos y la fecha; on board = de acuerdo con el plan.

ensenanza.en: We will support you with a clear guide and an experienced buddy, and I want to address a concern that several of you have raised.
ensenanza.es: Les apoyaremos con una guía clara y un compañero con experiencia, y quiero atender una preocupación que varios de ustedes han planteado.
ensenanza.nota: We will support you with + sustantivo: ofrece apoyo concreto; address a concern: atender lo que preocupa.

ensenanza.en: Good leaders explain the reason first and ask what would make it easier for everyone to adapt, because buy-in grows from questions.
ensenanza.es: Los buenos líderes explican primero el motivo y preguntan qué facilitaría la adaptación de todos, porque la adhesión nace de las preguntas.
ensenanza.nota: What would make it easier...?: pregunta de coaching para buscar la solución con la persona.

ensenanza.en: Some teething problems are normal in any new schedule, so please tell me quickly if a shift does not work for your families.
ensenanza.es: Algunos problemas iniciales son normales en cualquier horario nuevo, así que avísame pronto si un turno no funciona para tus familias.
ensenanza.nota: Teething problems: dificultades típicas al empezar algo nuevo; se anticipan para que no sorprendan.

explicacion.titulo: Guiar a un equipo por un cambio
explicacion.texto: Al anunciar un cambio, sigue cuatro pasos: anuncia (I want to announce...), explica el motivo (The reason is...), presenta el plan (Here is the plan...) y ofrece apoyo (We will support you with...). Después atiende las preocupaciones: reconócelas (I understand your concern), refléjalas (It sounds like you feel...) y pregunta (What would make it easier?). Esta clase de cierre integra lo del bloque: lenguaje de ánimo, preguntas de coaching y retroalimentación clara.

formula.texto: The reason is that more families are coming,
we will support you with a clear guide.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I want to announce you a change.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I want to announce a change.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Announce no se usa con persona directa; se dice announce a change (to the team) o tell you about a change.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I understand your concerns about to work earlier.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I understand your concern about working earlier.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de una preposición (about) va -ing, no to + infinitivo.

situacion.contexto: Mia, coordinadora de un huerto comunitario, anuncia un cambio de horario a Tom.

dialogo.texto: I want to announce a change. The reason is that more families are coming.
dialogo.traduccion: Quiero anunciar un cambio. El motivo es que vienen más familias.

dialogo.texto: Does that mean I must work earlier? I study at night.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Eso significa que tengo que trabajar más temprano? Yo estudio por la noche.

dialogo.texto: I understand your concern. What would make it easier for you?
dialogo.traduccion: Entiendo tu preocupación. ¿Qué haría que te resultara más fácil?

dialogo.texto: Maybe the afternoon shift.
dialogo.traduccion: Quizá el turno de la tarde.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿cómo responde Mia a la preocupación de Tom?

opciones.es: La reconoce y le hace una pregunta de coaching sobre qué le resultaría más fácil.
Le dice que el turno de la mañana es obligatorio para todos.
Le pide que deje el grupo hasta que termine sus estudios.

item.feedback: Mia dice «I understand your concern» y pregunta «What would make it easier for you?»: reconoce y pregunta, sin imponer.

filas.texto: The reason is that more families are coming.
Here is the plan: two shifts instead of one.
We will support you with a clear guide.
I understand your concern. What would help?

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase del anuncio explica la razón del cambio?
guiada.feedback: «The reason is...» introduce el porqué; las otras frases presentan el plan y el apoyo.
opciones: The reason is that more families are coming to the garden.
Here is the plan: one morning shift and one afternoon shift.
Everybody will get a clear guide and a buddy in the first week.
guiada.pista: Busca la frase que empieza con The reason is.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «¿Qué te facilitaría empezar más temprano?»
guiada.feedback: What would make it easier...? es la pregunta de coaching que busca lo que ayudaría a la persona.
guiada.texto: Tom studies at night, so the morning shift worries him. The coordinator asks: What would make it ___ for you to start earlier?
guiada.pista: Es el comparativo de easy: termina en -ier.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Te apoyaremos con una guía clara.»
guiada.feedback: Support you with + sustantivo ofrece un apoyo concreto dentro del anuncio.
guiada.respuesta: We will support you with a clear guide
guiada.pista: Empieza por We will support y termina con el recurso.

practica.consigna: Escucha el anuncio y elige qué razón da la coordinadora para el cambio.
practica.feedback: La razón es que vienen más familias y hace falta más tiempo para recibirlas.
practica.audio: On Saturday morning, the coordinator of a community garden spoke to the volunteers to tell them about a change. Starting next month, she said, there will be two shifts instead of one, because more families are coming and we need more time to welcome them. She explained that each volunteer would choose a shift by Friday, and that a guide and a buddy would support anyone who felt unsure. One volunteer asked whether the early shift was required. The coordinator smiled and asked: What would make it easier for you to come in the morning?
opciones: More families are coming, so they need more time to welcome them.
Volunteers have asked for shorter hours on Saturdays so that they can rest.
The garden will close earlier on Saturdays from next year.

practica.consigna: Con el mismo anuncio, elige con qué propósito pregunta la coordinadora al voluntario.
practica.feedback: La pregunta de coaching invita al voluntario a buscar una solución con ella, en lugar de imponerle una.
practica.audio: On Saturday morning, the coordinator of a community garden spoke to the volunteers to tell them about a change. Starting next month, she said, there will be two shifts instead of one, because more families are coming and we need more time to welcome them. She explained that each volunteer would choose a shift by Friday, and that a guide and a buddy would support anyone who felt unsure. One volunteer asked whether the early shift was required. The coordinator smiled and asked: What would make it easier for you to come in the morning?
opciones: To involve the volunteer in finding a solution.
To check that he understands the new rules.
To persuade him to cancel his other plans.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Quiero anunciar un cambio en nuestro horario de los sábados.»
practica.feedback: Announce a change abre el mensaje de forma clara; no lleva persona directa (announce you).
practica.texto: Thank you all for coming this morning. I want to ___ a change in our Saturday schedule, and I want to explain why.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe el anuncio del cambio a los voluntarios.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen anuncio da la razón, el plan y el apoyo, reconoce cada preocupación y responde con una pregunta de coaching.
evaluacion.texto: Eres coordinador de un huerto comunitario. Los sábados habrá dos turnos (9–12 y 12–15) porque vienen más familias. Tom estudia de noche y le preocupa el turno de la mañana; Ana teme no saber usar el nuevo registro. Escribe el anuncio (unas 220–270 palabras): razón del cambio, plan en pasos, apoyo y una respuesta con pregunta de coaching a cada preocupación.
evaluacion.respuesta:
Hi everyone,
Thank you for coming. I want to announce a change in our Saturday schedule. The reason is simple: more families are coming to the garden, and we need more time to help them.
Here is the plan. First, we will have two shifts instead of one: nine to twelve, and twelve to three. Second, each volunteer will choose a shift by Friday. Third, we will review the plan in a month.
We will support you with a clear guide and a buddy for your first week. Nobody will work alone.
Tom, I understand your concern about the early start. It sounds like you feel stressed because you study at night. What would make the afternoon shift easier for you?
Ana, I hear that you are worried about the new register. What would help you feel more confident? I can practise it with you on Thursday.
I know change is tough, but I am proud of what this team does every week. Thank you for your effort, and please tell me what you think.
aceptadas:
Dear volunteers,
I want to announce a change for Saturdays. The reason is that many more families are coming to the garden, and our morning is now too short.
This is the plan. We will work in two shifts, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. Each of you can choose the shift that suits you best. We will review the schedule after four weeks, and then we will decide together if we keep it.
Of course, we will support you. You will receive a short guide, and an experienced volunteer will help you during the first week.
Tom, I understand your concern. You study at night, so the early start is hard. What would make the afternoon shift possible for you?
Ana, it sounds like you feel worried about the new register. What could we try so that you feel more confident? I am happy to practise it with you.
Change is never easy, but your effort makes a real difference. Thank you for your patience and your ideas.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué actitud adopta la coordinadora ante la queja de la voluntaria.
evaluacion.feedback: La coordinadora reconoce la queja («That is fair») y pide ideas: no defiende la decisión ni la cancela.
evaluacion.audio: After the announcement, one volunteer stayed behind. I am not against the change, she told the coordinator, but nobody asked us before deciding. The coordinator did not defend the decision. She said: It sounds like you feel left out of the process, and you need to be heard earlier. That is fair. What would make it easier to give you a voice next time? The volunteer relaxed and said she would join the new shift.
opciones: She accepts the criticism of the process and asks for ideas.
She insists that the decision was made in a fair way.
She offers to cancel the change for this volunteer.

evaluacion.consigna: Con la misma escena, elige qué se deduce del final de la conversación.
evaluacion.feedback: La voluntaria se relaja al sentirse escuchada y acepta el turno: su queja era sobre el proceso, no sobre el horario.
evaluacion.audio: After the announcement, one volunteer stayed behind. I am not against the change, she told the coordinator, but nobody asked us before deciding. The coordinator did not defend the decision. She said: It sounds like you feel left out of the process, and you need to be heard earlier. That is fair. What would make it easier to give you a voice next time? The volunteer relaxed and said she would join the new shift.
opciones: Her concern was more about being heard than about the shift itself.
She had not understood the reason for the change until that moment.
She joined the new shift only because she had no choice.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «La coordinadora quiere que todos se sumen al plan antes del primer turno.»
evaluacion.feedback: Get everyone on board significa conseguir que todos se sumen y apoyen el plan.
evaluacion.texto: The new plan will only work if the whole team supports it. Before the first shift, the coordinator wants to get everyone on ___.

repaso.consigna: Lee el correo y elige qué incluye y qué omite el anuncio.
repaso.feedback: El correo explica el porqué, da el plan y el apoyo (guía y compañero), pero no invita a expresar preocupaciones.
opciones: It explains why, gives the plan and the support, but invites no concerns.
It gives the plan and the explanation, but offers no support at all.
It explains the plan and the support, but never says why.
repaso.texto: Dear volunteers, from March the garden will open for two shifts on Saturdays, because many more families now visit us. You will receive a short guide, and a buddy will help you during your first week.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué cambió la actitud de la voluntaria.
repaso.feedback: Lo que cambió su actitud fue la pregunta de la coordinadora: sentir que su opinión contaba.
repaso.audio: A new volunteer told her friend: At first I hated the two shifts. Then the coordinator said she understood my worry and asked what would help me. Nobody had ever asked me that. In the end I chose the afternoon, and I felt that my opinion counted. That single question turned my doubts into interest.
opciones: Feeling listened to when the coordinator asked what would help her.
Getting the shift that she had wanted from the first day.
Receiving a guide that explained the new schedule in detail.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Antes del plan, explica siempre el motivo del cambio.»
repaso.feedback: The reason for the change va antes del plan: quien entiende el porqué acepta mejor el cómo.
repaso.texto: People accept a new schedule more easily when they understand why. Before you present the plan, always explain the ___ for the change.
